public_comment.topic: Asked whether fee increases will be repeated yearly with expenses or whether there is a long-term plan; also remarked that academics was named priority one and athletics second.

Asked about a per-sport cost breakdown requested last week; argued a roughly 30% jump hurts middle-income families who don't qualify for reduced lunch or waivers and may reduce participation and fund revenue.
Asked what participation data will be released (baseline from prior years) and what other mechanisms could help close the equity gap, including for families who don't fill out low-income forms.
Asked about participation counts, enrollment, and how many participations are unique students versus counted per season; suggested granular data on families dropping from three sports to two.
Asked what happens if fees are not raised; raised the town's limited levers for revenue generation, and noted Parks is considering fee increases for youth baseball/softball.

budget_items.topic: Athletic user fees share of program funding
budget_items.what_was_said: Parents through user fees fund about a quarter of the total athletic program, later described as about 26%.
A neighboring town charges a per-sport per-season fee with a high school family cap; Brookfield offers only three sports.
Transportation, coaching stipends and MIAA official fees are rising; stipends rose this year and will rise again next year.

budget_items.topic: Proposed athletic fee for first student
budget_items.what_was_said: Proposed fee for the first student in the family per season with sibling discounts and a family cap extending grades six through twelve; still open to discussion.
Revolving account revenue is not matching expenses; goal is to zero the account down each year rather than stockpile.
A participant compared potential full-pay fee revenue to what FY24 combined fees brought in; participation counts are student-seasons, not unique students.

budget_items.topic: Town manager's budget guidance for schools
budget_items.what_was_said: The district must fit its budget within a projected increase over last year, which does not keep pace with costs; painful cuts to be proposed the next night.
Uncertainty about federal grant funding could reduce district funding.
Chair said turf and track complex project costs might be offset through cell towers and solar, and a sponsorship policy might be opened.
A commenter described the proposed increase as a large jump for middle-income families.

decisions.decision: Per-sport cost breakdown was not released at this meeting; release would require action by the superintendent or school committee, and the chair noted reservations.
Commentary from the meeting will be brought back to the school committee and administration for further consideration.
Council will hold an annual meeting at the end of summer rather than meeting every season (stated as earlier agreed).
Athletic director to try to obtain the unique-student participation count and share it if found.

meetings.headline: Athletic Advisory Council heard a proposal to raise athletic user fees; no vote was taken and feedback goes to the School Committee.
meetings.summary: The council met by Zoom to present one proposal to raise athletic user fees, with a cap for families across grades 7-12, and to take feedback from parents. The administration said costs for transportation, coaching stipends and officials are rising and the athletic revolving account ran negative last year. No votes were scheduled or taken; feedback will be reported to the School Committee as part of the budget process.

minutes.headline: Athletic Advisory Council heard a proposal to raise athletic user fees; no vote was taken and feedback goes to the School Committee.
minutes.summary: The council met by Zoom to present one proposal to raise athletic user fees, with a cap for families across grades 7-12, and to take feedback from parents. The administration said costs for transportation, coaching stipends and officials are rising and the athletic revolving account ran negative last year. No votes were scheduled or taken; feedback will be reported to the School Committee as part of the budget process.

public_comment.topic: A parent of two middle schoolers estimated the combined monthly cost of sports and other activities, questioned fairness of a flat fee for a sport with few meets, and asked why the district does not buy its own bus.
Argued a roughly 30% one-year fee jump is too large and asked about phasing increases in smaller steps; suggested the fees reduce the annual budget share rather than add to it.
Asked for a better breakdown of the costs of each sport to understand equity, supported paying coaches and referees better, and noted the bus company's monopoly.
Asked to see what each sport costs and why other places seem to get grants and funding so students do not pay fees.
Asked about youth sports and field rental fees, the local budget contribution to athletics, and what the fee increase avoids; did back-of-napkin math on net revenue after assumed participation loss.
Asked whether adding more teams would bring in more fees and said information about middle school sports and sign-ups is hard to find.
Asked about gate receipts collected at games and whether cell tower lease money is used for field maintenance.
Asked whether the district talks to neighboring towns without fees, and noted that booster parents are the same parents paying fees.
Suggested sponsorship and advertising revenue and combining middle and high school into one family cap.
Asked about grants for athletics and whether the grant-writing position discussed during the override was filled.

budget_items.what_was_said: The chair said projected costs and confident revenue for next year are about four million apart and will narrow but not close.
The chair said Chapter 70 funds a share of the operating budget but grows much more slowly than costs.
Transportation, coaching stipends and official fees are rising.
High school full pay fee for the first student and middle school fee were described.
Brookfield is around a set fee; Groton-Dunstable charges per sport per season with a family cap.
The district spent all of its local athletic expense budget, and the revolving account went negative by the end of last year.
User fees bring in a limited amount annually and offset a minority share of athletic expenses.
Proposal raises fees per sport per season for full pay, with sibling and reduced discounts and a family cap across seasons.
The cap was confirmed as yearly and per family.
A resident calculated what the increase would bring in and called the percentage rise large for one year.
The chair said a van might offset low-density transportation and that a bus costs a lot with a short regulatory life.
figures_as_heard: a quarter of a million dollar

budget_items.what_was_said: Transportation and coaching salaries were moved back into the local budget; fees may fund officials.
Gate receipts were noted and the athletic director explained which games charge admission.

budget_items.topic: Cell tower lease for turf field
budget_items.what_was_said: The original intent was to offset the bond for the turf field; the field is still being paid off and needs replacement.
A town-funded grant writer position suggested by the finance committee never came to fruition as far as the chair knew.
A resident estimated net gain with a participation loss; the administration said the maximum figure assumes no loss.

decisions.decision: Feedback will be reported back to the School Committee; a follow-on version of this conversation was announced for next Tuesday at six o'clock.
The proposed family cap is yearly and per family, and the cap would cover grades 7 through 12 together.
Coaching stipend rates, set in the Lea contract, will be made available.
The chair will post the presentation link in the chat; added slides to be posted.
Dr Gilson will get back to a resident with the amount the district budget contributes to athletics.

what_happened.line: The Athletic Advisory Council heard one proposal to raise athletic user fees, with a yearly per-family cap covering grades 7 through 12 together; no vote was taken.
The administration said transportation, coaching stipends and official fees are rising, and the athletic revolving account ran negative by the end of last year.
Parents and residents questioned the size of a one-year increase, asked about phasing it in, and asked for a cost breakdown by sport.
Transportation and coaching salaries were moved back into the local budget; fees may fund officials.
Feedback will be reported to the School Committee, and a follow-on session was announced for the following Tuesday at six o'clock.

why_it_matters: If the School Committee adopts the proposal, families with children in sports would pay higher fees per sport per season, limited by a yearly family cap across grades 7-12.
The fees sit inside a larger budget gap for next year, which the chair described as narrowing but not closing, so the same pressure may reach other lines.
